_about: The joy hub (plan 7.6f), built to the level of love and righteousness. Rows as in love.json and righteousness.json: a noun row by the words in the noun's own phrase or verse, a verb row by who rejoices (the frames) and the words in its own clause, a pick row by hand where the text itself names the one it is about or where no rule can read what the verses say. 'match: all' -- a verse sits in every row it fits. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/joy.json. NOT SHOWN until reviewed. CONSOLIDATED 2026-10-10 from 65 rows to 26 (brief rule 8: about 15-25, love has 22): rows that said the same thing are merged and each merged row's _why names what it came from; every verse stays placed.

titles.noun: What the text says of joy

_words_why: The card lists six nouns (שִׂמְחָה χαρά שָׂשׂוֹן מָשׂוֹשׂ חֶדְוָה גִּילָה); the verbs of the same families are words too, as the owner said: שָׂמַח and the adjective שָׂמֵחַ with שִׂמְחָה; שׂוּשׂ with שָׂשׂוֹן and מָשׂוֹשׂ; גִּיל with גִּילָה and the noun גִּיל (h1524, 'gladness', 6 verses the card did not list); חָדָה with חֶדְוָה; χαίρω and συγχαίρω with χαρά. The Greek words that render them are rightly together (the Greek Old Testament renders גיל by ἀγαλλιάω and שמח by εὐφραίνω): ἀγαλλιάω and ἀγαλλίασις, εὐφραίνω. Each verse keeps the word it uses (the example shows it), so no verse is handed over as the other word. ORDER MATTERS: h1523 (the verb גִּיל) stands before h1524 (the noun גִּיל) because the builder keys a word by its pointed lemma and the later one wins; with the noun last, the noun is found in the noun rows and the verb is found by its form. The Aramaic חֶדְוָה (h2305, Ezra 6:16) has the same spelling as h2304 and would shadow it, so it is left in 'others'.
_sense_why: Measured on the words' in-verse glosses (2026-10-10): χαίρω as 'Greetings' (6) and 'Hail' (3) is the greeting, not joy (Acts 15:23, Jas 1:1, Matt 28:9, Matt 27:29 ...) and falls away by itself. 'delight', 'pleasure', 'enjoy', 'mirth', 'gaiety' are how the Berean renders שִׂמְחָה / שׂוּשׂ / מָשׂוֹשׂ in Eccl 2:1-2, 8:15, Deut 28:63, Isa 65:18 -- the same Hebrew word, so they stay. 'gloat' and 'glee' are שָׂמַח at an enemy's fall (Lam 2:17, Ps 35:15): the word is the joy word and the text is the text. 'welcomed' (Isa 39:2) is dropped as another sense. NOT CAUGHT BY THE SENSE: χαίρω in 2 John 10-11 is glossed 'to rejoice' but is the greeting idiom (χαίρειν λέγειν: 'greet'); the Berean prints 'greet'. They are held out of every row by hand and stand under 'More'.

1Chr.12.41.why: the Hebrew's 12:41 ('there was joy in Israel') is printed in the Berean's 12:40; 12:41 as shown has no text

Ps.13.5.why: the Hebrew's 13:5 ('my foes rejoice when I fall') is the Berean's 13:4: the Berean sets the title outside verse 1, the Hebrew counts it as verse 1

Ps.13.6.why: the Hebrew's 13:6 ('my heart will rejoice in Your salvation') is the Berean's 13:5; the Berean splits the Hebrew 13:6 into its 13:5 and 13:6

others._why: Doug, 2026-10-09 (love): the rows stand on the concept's own words and their counterparts; a different word the English also calls joy is named apart with its verses. רָנַן 'sing for joy', עָלַז / עָלַץ 'exult', εὐφροσύνη are different words. The regex does not take 'gladly' (ἡδέως, an adverb: 'gladly listened') or 'jubilee' (יוֹבֵל, a year).
others.title: Other words translated “joy”, “rejoice”, “exult”

g2744.note: The Greek is καυχάομαι, “to boast”; the Berean prints “rejoice” or “exult” in these four verses. A different word from the joy words above, named apart.

others._add_why: The panel named the gap: Rom 5:3 ("we also rejoice in our sufferings") is among the most-sought joy verses and the word is not found by the gloss rule (καυχάομαι is 'boast' in most of its 36 verses). Different word, so apart, never in the rows.

rows.label: The joy of the LORD, and joy God gives: in His presence, in His word
rows.note: The text's own phrase "the joy of the LORD" (Neh 8:10), kept as written: where readers part on whether it is the joy He has or the joy He gives, the page does not choose.
rows._why: MERGED 2026-10-10 from four rows: 'The joy of the LORD, of God' (rule: the divine name next to the noun; 2 verses), 'Joy God gives' (17), 'Joy in the presence of the LORD, of God' (9), 'Joy and the word, the testimonies' (7). All by hand, as the divine persons are: verses where the text itself says the LORD or God gives, fills, restores or anoints with joy, sets joy before Him, or makes His word the joy. Ps 4:7, 16:11, 21:6, 30:11, 51:8, 51:12 are addressed to the LORD ('You') in a prayer whose own opening names Him; the panel may read them as that. Heb 1:9 (the oil of joy) is the Berean's 'God, Your God'. 'The word' is λόγος and דָּבָר, and דָּבָר is also 'matter' in every other verse a rule would find, so no rule. A rule on פָּנֶה would take Prov 15:13 ('a cheerful countenance'). PANEL FIXES: Isa 9:3 out ('You' is not named near enough; it stays in the victory and feasts rows); the rocky-ground hearers (Mark 4:16, Matt 13:20, Luke 8:13) out, since they say only that the hearer receives the word with joy (they stand in the catch-all, Luke 8:13 also in 'Joy and sorrow' and 'Joy beside ... faith'); relabelled so that the label no longer chooses between the joy He has and the joy He gives.
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Joy and the Holy Spirit
rows.note: Each verse names the Spirit or the fruit of the Spirit beside joy, as the text has them; the page says no more than the verses do.
rows._why: by hand: the Spirit is a divine person, decided record by record; verses where the text itself names the Holy Spirit, or 'the fruit of the Spirit', beside joy

rows.label: The joy of Jesus
rows._why: by hand: 'My joy' said by Jesus (John 15:11, 17:13) and 'the joy set before Him' where the verse names Jesus (Heb 12:2)

rows.label: Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents
rows.note: The text's own words, kept as written; where Christian traditions part on how repentance comes about or what accompanies it, the page takes no side.
rows._why: SPLIT (panel): Luke 15:7, 15:10 only -- repentance is flagged high by the committee, so the no-side note stays and covers exactly these two verses.

rows.label: “Enter into the joy of your master”; joy and the kingdom
rows.note: The text's own words, kept as written: whose joy "the master's" is, and what the joy is beyond what the verse says, the page does not decide.
rows._why: SPLIT (panel): the master's joy (Matt 25:21, 23), a man's joy at the treasure of the kingdom of heaven (Matt 13:44) and joy in the kingdom of God (Rom 14:17, which is also in 'Joy and the Holy Spirit'); the examples show the kingdom part.

rows.label: Joy and salvation, rescue, victory: the redeemed, the good news, a king enthroned
rows._why: MERGED from 'Joy and salvation, good news, the redeemed' (7, rule on the salvation words) and 'Joy at a victory, a rescue, a king enthroned' (8, picks). The first row's verses are kept as the rule found them. Judg 16:23 is the Philistines' joy over Samson, kept: hard verses stay.
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Joy beside peace, love, hope and faith; joy filled, full, complete

not_verses.Jer.33.9: שָׁלוֹם is rendered 'prosperity' here; the verse names no peace

rows._add_why: love: a rule on love words took Prov 21:17 ('loves pleasure'), Isa 66:10 ('all who love her') and Ps 45:7 ('loved righteousness'); these five set love beside joy by hand
rows._why: MERGED from four rows: 'Joy and peace', 'Joy, hope and faith', 'Joy and love', 'Joy filled, full, complete' (one rule on the union of their words; love by `add`). Set side by side with no priority among peace, love, hope and faith (love was flagged medium by the committee for the faith/love order). The earlier exclusions of Gal 5:22 (πίστις = 'faithfulness') and 2 John 12 ('I hope to come') no longer matter: Gal 5:22 stands here for peace and love, 2 John 12 for 'our joy may be complete'.

rows.label: Joy and sorrow: trial, affliction, mourning, weeping; joy taken away, ended

not_verses.Heb.12.11: λύπη is printed 'painful' (discipline), so the verse names no mourning or grief in the Berean's words

rows._add_why: 'joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property' (Heb 10:34) names no word a rule reads; and the 17 'joy taken away, ended' verses (Isa 16:10, 24:8, 24:11, 32:13-14, Jer 7:34, 16:9, 25:10, 48:33, 49:25, Joel 1:12, 1:16, Hos 2:11, Lam 5:15, Ezek 24:25, Job 20:5, Jas 4:9): no word a rule could read means 'ended'; each says the joy is removed, has ceased, left, turned to gloom or is momentary
rows._why: MERGED from three rows: 'Joy and trial, affliction, suffering' (rule), 'Joy and mourning, sorrow, weeping, grief' (rule), 'Joy taken away, ended' (picks, now `add`). Joy and its opposite in one row.

rows.label: Joy weighed: pleasure and mirth; the righteous and the wicked, fools and sinners
rows._why: MERGED from 'Joy, pleasure and mirth weighed' (7 picks: 'what does it accomplish?', 'joy may end in sorrow', 'momentary', 'the house of pleasure') and 'Joy, the righteous, the wicked, fools and sinners' (8, rule on those words), now by hand with the same verses. The label says what they weigh, not a verdict on joy: Eccl 9:7 and 5:20 are in 'Joy from the LORD'.
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Joy at feasts: food, wine, the harvest, the bride and bridegroom

not_verses.Jer.15.16: 'ate' is of the LORD's words, not a meal; the verse stands in 'Joy from the LORD'

rows._why: MERGED from 'Joy beside feasts, food, wine and the harvest' and 'The voice of joy and gladness, the bride and bridegroom' (both rules, one union): the occasions of a feast and a wedding.
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Joy with singing, music and dancing; in Zion, in Jerusalem; at the ark, the sacrifice, the altar

not_verses.Eccl.2.2: the match here is a homograph, הוֹלֵל 'folly'; the verse is about laughter and pleasure, not song
not_verses.Isa.61.7: the Hebrew has רנן ('shout for joy') but the Berean prints 'rejoice in their share'; no singing or shouting in the text shown
not_verses.Ps.45.15: הֵיכָל here is the king's palace, not the temple
not_verses.Song.3.11: the daughters of Zion are called out to see the king; the joy is the wedding day

rows._why: MERGED from three rules, one union: 'Joy with singing, shouting, music and dancing', 'Joy in Zion, in Jerusalem', 'Joy at the ark, the sacrifice, the altar' -- the places and the sound of worship. Ps 137:3 ('songs of joy') now stands here for the song, not for Zion.

rows.label: Every other use of the joy nouns
The LORD rejoices, delights
rows.note: Deut 28:63, among the covenant curses, sets the LORD's pleasure in making Israel prosper beside His pleasure in destroying them if they break the covenant; kept as the text has it.
rows._why: by hand: verses where the text itself names the LORD or God as the one who rejoices. Isa 65:19 and Jer 32:41 are the LORD speaking in the first person (Isa 65:13, Jer 32:42 say 'the Lord GOD says', 'this is what the LORD says' in the same speech); kept on Doug's decision, 2026-10-10. PANEL FIXES: Zech 4:10 out (it is 'these seven eyes of the LORD' that rejoice, a figure; the verse stays in 'Rejoice at what they see or hear'); the Deut 28:63 note now gives the verse's own 'just as ... so also' and the covenant setting.

rows.label: Jesus rejoiced
rows._why: by hand: Luke 10:21 'Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit'; John 11:15 'I am glad I was not there', Jesus speaking (v. 14)

rows.label: The LORD makes glad: made them glad; asked to make us glad
rows._why: MERGED from 'The LORD made them glad' (7) and 'Asked of the LORD: make us glad, revive us' (5), by hand: the LORD or God is the one who makes them rejoice (Ps 92:4 and 21:6 are addressed to Him: O LORD, v. 4; Your presence, v. 6), or is asked to (Ps 86:4 'O Lord', 90:14-15 on the LORD's 'loving devotion', 85:6 'Will You not revive us', 51:8 'let me hear joy').

rows.label: Rejoice in the LORD, in God, in the Lord; before Him; in His salvation, His word, what He has done
rows.note: Where the text says "the Lord" (κύριος: Phil 3:1, 4:4, 4:10), readers take it of Christ or of the Father, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: MERGED from six rows, now by hand with the same verses as built and sampled: 'Rejoice in the LORD, in God' (22; a rule on the clause took 'wine that cheers both God and man' Judg 9:13, 'streams delight the city of God' Ps 46:4 and every verse where the LORD is the one rejoicing; the first fourteen name the LORD, God, the Most High or the Holy One of Israel in the verse, Ps 149:2 'their Maker', 'their King'; Ps 5:11, 33:21, 40:16, 66:6, 89:16 say 'in You', 'in Him', 'in Your name' of the LORD the psalm addresses -- the panel may read them as that), 'Rejoice in the Lord' (3), 'Rejoice before the LORD your God' (9: 'before the LORD', 'in the presence of the LORD your God', 'before God' / 'before You'), 'Rejoice at what the LORD, God has done or given' (7), 'Rejoice in salvation' (7, rule on the clause, Phil 1:18 and 1 Pet 1:8 out because the clause runs into the next verse), 'Joy in the word, the testimonies, the precepts' (3, Ps 19:8 by `add` before). John 20:20 ('when they saw the Lord') is a sight, in 'Rejoice at what they see or hear'.
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Rejoice over what was lost and found
rows.note: The text's own parables, kept as written; the page takes no side on how Christian traditions apply them to repentance.

rows.label: Who rejoices: the righteous, the upright, the humble, Zion and Jerusalem, the heart, the heavens and the earth
rows._why: MERGED from four rows (rules on the frames' agent, on Zion/Jerusalem in the verse, and a pick): 'The righteous, the upright, the humble, the servants rejoice' (14; Isa 65:13 and Ps 109:28 'servants' by `add`: a rule on עֶבֶד took 'your menservants and maidservants' in the Deuteronomy feast lists), 'Zion and Jerusalem: rejoiced in, told to rejoice' (15), 'The heart, the soul, the spirit rejoices' (12; Isa 66:14 out, the Berean prints 'you will rejoice'), 'The heavens, the earth, the land, the wilderness rejoice' (8, by hand).
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Rejoicing together: the household, the people, rejoice with others; “I rejoice” over you; in the truth
rows._why: MERGED from five rows: 'Rejoice together: the household, the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, the widow' (6; Exod 4:14 and Isa 9:17 out: Aaron 'the Levite' is a brother, and the Lord has no compassion on fatherless and widows), 'Rejoice with' (7; 1 Cor 13:6 is συγχαίρω but the Berean prints 'rejoices in the truth', so it stands in the truth), 'The people, the assembly, the city, the crowd rejoice' (19, rule on the agent), 'I rejoice over those he writes to' (16; the frames give Paul as agent in some verses and patient in others, so by hand), 'Rejoice in the truth' (3).
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Told to rejoice, and told not to

not_verses.Ps.35.19: a prayer that enemies not rejoice
not_verses.Ps.35.24: a prayer that enemies not rejoice
not_verses.Lam.4.21: a taunt to Edom, not an exhortation
not_verses.Job.3.6: a curse on the night; the Berean prints no 'rejoice'
not_verses.Ps.86.4: a prayer to the Lord: bring joy
not_verses.Ps.90.15: a prayer to the LORD: make us glad
not_verses.Prov.27.11: 'bring joy to my heart' bids the son cause joy, not rejoice
not_verses.Prov.23.25: a wish for the parents' joy, not a command to rejoice
not_verses.1Pet.1.8: states that they rejoice; the frames read it as a command
not_verses.Judg.9.19: a conditional wish ('then may you rejoice in Abimelech')
not_verses.Luke.12.19: the rich fool talking to himself ('Eat, drink, and be merry'), not a command anyone gives; stands in 'Everyday joy'

rows._why: MERGED from 'Told to rejoice' (rule: the frames' stance 'command') and 'Told not to rejoice' (7 picks). The prohibitions (Hos 9:1, Isa 14:29, Ezek 7:12, Prov 24:17, Obad 12, Mic 7:8, and Luke 10:20, which forbids one joy and commands another) are commands too, so the rule now takes them and they are no longer excluded. Still excluded: prayers that enemies not rejoice (Ps 35:19, 35:24), a taunt (Lam 4:21), a curse (Job 3:6), prayers to the Lord (Ps 86:4, 90:15), 'bring joy to my heart' (Prov 27:11), a wish for the parents (Prov 23:25), a statement (1 Pet 1:8), a conditional wish (Judg 9:19). PANEL FIXES: the nine Torah festival commands added by hand; Luke 12:19 out; note added.
rows._add_why: the Torah's festival commands, 'you shall rejoice before the LORD' (panel): the largest body of commanded joy in the Hebrew Scriptures, which the stance rule did not take (the Hebrew verb is projection-stance in the frames)
rows.note: The commands and the prohibitions each name what to rejoice in or not; the prohibitions are about particular joys (an enemy's fall, Prov 24:17, Obad 12, Mic 7:8), not about joy as such.

rows.label: Rejoice at what they see or hear
rows._why: by hand: each verse says they saw or heard, and rejoiced. A rule on 'see' and 'hear' took Eccl 3:22 ('I have seen'), Ps 90:15 ('years we have seen evil') and Ps 51:8 ('let me hear')

rows.label: Rejoicing in suffering and persecution; rejoicing and weeping together
rows._why: MERGED from two rules, one union: 'Rejoice in trials, suffering, persecution' and 'Rejoice and weep, mourn, grieve' (λυπέω was already out of the first so that John 16:20 and 2 Cor 6:10 would not read as rejoicing in trials; they stand here for sorrow). PANEL FIXES: five verses out (Lam 1:21, Hos 10:5, Prov 10:1, 17:21, 29:2 -- none says anyone rejoices in trial); relabelled descriptively, not as a bidding.

not_verses.Lam.1.21: the enemies are glad at the speaker's trouble; stands in 'Rejoicing over another's fall'
not_verses.Hos.10.5: mourners over an idol 'who rejoiced in its glory'; stands in the wealth and idol part of the fall row
not_verses.Prov.10.1: a wise son's joy against a foolish son's grief; stands in 'Everyday joy'
not_verses.Prov.17.21: a fool's father has no joy; stands in 'Everyday joy'
not_verses.Prov.29.2: the people rejoice when the righteous flourish; stands in 'Rejoicing together'

rows.label: Everyday joy: one's work, one's household (a wife, a son); wine, oil and a good word; making merry at a feast
rows._why: MERGED from five pick rows: Ecclesiastes' 'rejoice in his labor', 'in them all', 'while you are young' and Prov 5:18 (7); 'Rejoice in a wife, over a bride' (Deut 24:5, Song 1:4, Isa 62:5; 4); a son or a child brings joy (Proverbs, Jer 20:15, Luke 1:14, 2 John 4; 11); 'What makes glad' (the subject that gladdens is a thing, not a person: Ps 104:15, Judg 9:13, Prov 27:9, 12:25, 15:30, Ps 19:8, 45:8, 46:4; 9); 'Make merry, celebrate with a feast' (εὐφραίνω 'be merry' and the Hebrew 'wine makes life merry'; Rev 11:10 is the same word in a celebration over the two witnesses, kept; Acts 7:41 was taken out in the sample check: rejoicing at an idol's sacrifice, not a feast; 9). PANEL FIXES: Rev 11:10 out (the earth-dwellers gloating over the witnesses is no everyday joy; it stays in the fall row); a note on the warning cases; lead now shows work, household, wine and oil, and the feast (the son, Prov 10:1, is the fifth example).
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four
rows.note: Includes merry-making the text sets against itself or against its makers (Luke 12:19, 16:19, Job 21:12); the label names only what is done.

rows.label: Rejoicing over another's fall or ruin, at judgment; in wealth, an idol, plunder, evil
rows.note: Kept as the text has it, including where the righteous rejoice at the judgment of the wicked (Ps 58:10, 97:8, Rev 18:20); the page takes no side.
rows._why: MERGED from three rows: 'Rejoicing over another's fall or ruin' (17 picks: those who forbid it, describe it, pray against it; Ezek 35:14 out, it juxtaposes without saying 'over'), 'Rejoice at judgment, at being avenged' (4, rule on the clause + Ps 58:10), 'Rejoicing in wealth, an idol, plunder, evil' (Job 31:25, Hos 10:5, Acts 7:41, Jer 50:11, Hos 7:3, Hab 1:15; 6). The text's own objects of the joy, side by side.
rows._lead_why: examples chosen so that each part of the merged label is shown in the first four

rows.label: Every other use: rejoice, be glad, exult
rows.note: In John 5:35 and Prov 13:9 the Greek and Hebrew words are the ordinary ones for "rejoice", which the Berean renders otherwise ("bask", "shines brightly").
rows._why: 2 John 10-11 and Job 3:6 are out of the concept by `sense_drop`. John 5:35 and Prov 13:9 stay: the original word is the joy word there (ἀγαλλιάω, שָׂמַח 'rejoices') and only the Berean rewords. PANEL FIX: Job 3:6 is not secure -- most translations and commentators read the verb as 'be joined' (a night not joined to the days of the year), the Berean has no joy word, and a curse on the night in a hub of joy on a minority parse would mislead.

rows.label: Glad, joyful, rejoicing: of heart; the people at a king, a feast; and over another's calamity
rows._why: MERGED from four rows into the form's one row (21 verses of שָׂמֵחַ): a glad heart (7), the people glad at a king, a feast, a dedication (8), 'gloats over calamity' / 'rejoice in the twistedness of evil' (Prov 17:5, Ps 35:26, Prov 2:14; 3), and the rest. The three calamity verses are named in the 'Rejoicing over another's fall' verb row.
